title: When Is a Memory Safe Enough to Act On? Action-Conditioned Verification for Long-Lived Agents

object.carrier: Persistent memory claims with provenance (write time, source, supporting observation, recorded confidence) held in a memory graph G_M; instantiated as agent memory in ToolSandbox/AppWorld simulators with a hidden perturbation applied between sessions

safety_property.statement: A stale or wrong memory premise must not turn into a harmful action: before each candidate commit, the gate must either re-verify the action's memory premises, proceed only when the expected-loss and posterior harm-probability screens hold, or abstain (decline without verifying at high consequence). Failure condition: executing a commit on a false premise (wrong recipient, policy violation, task failure). Judged by Gate harmful rate and Unsafe Pass rate over Gate-evaluable instances, with safe-proceed recall and Proceed coverage reported alongside so safety is not bought by declining everything.
safety_property.operationalized_as: Gate harmful rate = harmful executions over all Gate-evaluable instances; Unsafe Pass rate (harmful-candidate analogue); safe-proceed recall (fraction of ground-truth-safe Gate-evaluable candidates executed); Proceed coverage; all measured by ToolSandbox/AppWorld native state-based evaluators rather than LLM judgment.

capabilities: Non-adversarial memory staleness: hidden environment perturbations drawn from ten families (V0-V9) spanning no change, single and multiple critical changes, irrelevant and correlated changes, unverifiable premises, noisy (r=0.9 or 0.7) and contradictory verifiers, cost-inverted verifier sets, and misleading source trust (trust 0.95 while the world is stale)
Memory claims can be stale, contradicted, or missing while retaining plausible provenance and recorded confidence
Some action premises have no available verifier; verifier sets can pair a cheap noisy channel with an expensive reliable one
assumptions: Simulator ground truth is never injected into memory; history sessions write only tool-observed or user-supplied facts
Verifier costs, reliabilities, and availability are explicit and held fixed across methods; environment replay is deterministic from snapshot and seed
The gate sees only the agent's information set: unperturbed and single-critical-change instances are indistinguishable before the first verification
An executable consequence signal or explicit policy specification exists to define the asymmetric loss L
not_covered: Adversarial attacks: no memory poisoning, prompt injection, or adversary writing to memory is modeled
Cross-user or multi-agent tampering with shared memory
Real irreversible consequences outside simulator scoring (reputational damage, downstream human cost, delayed effects)
Premise completeness, calibration correctness, and observation-model correctness (oracle guarantees scoped in Appendix C.2)

intervention.name: AMV-Guard
intervention.description: An action-conditioned verification gate between planner and executor. For each candidate commit it: (1) extracts the action's premises (direct/transitive/joint) via an LLM extractor plus a public tool-contract rule layer with a counterfactual relevance filter; (2) estimates calibrated memory-error probabilities per supporting claim (logistic base model + Platt/beta/bounded-isotonic calibration over recency, source, consistency, graph position, and model-confidence features) and converts them to action-precondition violation probabilities; (3) applies a screened stopping value (expected-loss threshold delta, posterior harm-probability limit epsilon, abstention cost kappa); (4) selects checks by greedy one-step VOI with a bounded two-step fallback, re-deciding after each observation. If a required premise is invalidated (posterior violation probability above rho), the gate returns ReplanRequired instead of executing the stale candidate. Theoretical core: Proposition 1 shows increasing action consequence can move the same memory through proceed, verify, and direct-abstain regimes.

controls.name: AMV-Static (static verification policy given same calibrated beliefs, predicted dependencies, costs, reliabilities)

results.claim: On ToolSandbox (Qwen3.5-35B-A3B backbone, 3 observation seeds), adaptive action-conditioned verification (AMV-Guard) reduces mean verification cost by 33.9% vs AMV-Static given identical calibrated beliefs and predicted dependencies, while both methods retain 100% safe-proceed recall, 0% Unsafe Pass and 0% Gate harmful, buying 5.33 points more Proceed coverage and 1.56 points more task success at 0.21 points higher raw harm.
results.comparison: 100% safe-proceed recall, 0% Unsafe Pass, 0% Gate harmful retained; +5.33 points Proceed coverage, +1.56 points task success, +0.21 points raw harm
results.setting: ToolSandbox live end-to-end, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B backbone; 640 test instances x 3 observation seeds; per Table 4 (counts are train/development/test) the test split covers V0, V1, V2, and V5-V9 only — V3 (two critical changes) and V4 (correlated event) are 160/0/0 train/development/test, so the main test includes neither multi-critical-change nor correlated-change perturbations; AMV-Guard vs AMV-Static given same predicted dependencies, calibrated beliefs, verifier costs and reliabilities
results.quote: Relative to AMV-Static, it reduces cost by 33.9% while both methods retain 100% safe-proceed recall, 0% Unsafe Pass, and 0% Gate harmful. This saving accompanies 5.33 points more Proceed coverage and 1.56 points more task success, with raw harm 0.21 points higher.

denominator.n_total: 640 test instances per seed x 3 observation seeds
denominator.n_valid: Gate metrics (safe-proceed recall, Unsafe Pass, Gate harmful, Proceed coverage, verification cost): 600 Gate-evaluable per seed, 1,800 over three seeds; end-to-end metrics (task success, raw harm): all 640 test instances per seed, including the 40 with initial-candidate action or intent errors
denominator.how_counted: Section 5.1: the Gate metrics exclude the 40 test instances with initial-candidate action or intent errors, leaving 600 per seed and 1,800 over three seeds; task success is end-to-end, and raw harm records any executed action whose observed loss exceeds the threshold, including planning or intent failures

limitations.statement: Premise extraction is partly model-driven: the counterfactual filter cannot recover a premise never proposed, so extractor recall upper-bounds the whole pipeline.
limitations.quote: Premise extraction remains partly model-driven: the counterfactual procedure of Section 4.2 filters proposed premises but cannot recover one never proposed, so extractor recall upper-bounds the pipeline

limitations.statement: The deployed planner is a bounded approximation (one-step VOI plus depth-two fallback) and need not match the exact planner on longer complementary verification sequences.
limitations.quote: The deployed planner is a bounded approximation: it prefers any positive one-step VOI and invokes only a depth-two fallback when no such query exists, so it need not match the full exact planner on longer complementary sequences.

limitations.statement: The observation model uses binary support/refute outcomes with stated reliability; a verifier covering several premises produces one shared binary observation, an approximation rather than an exact joint observation model.
limitations.quote: The current ToolSandbox observation model uses binary support/refute outcomes with stated verifier reliability. A verifier covering several premises produces one shared binary observation

limitations.statement: The risk engine cannot represent several distinct joint hyperedges in one candidate (jointly marked premises share one latent draw).
limitations.quote: It therefore cannot represent several distinct joint hyperedges in one candidate.

limitations.statement: The loss function needs an executable consequence signal or explicit policy specification; where neither exists the asymmetry is hand-supplied, and sensitivity analysis characterises but does not remove that dependence.
limitations.quote: The loss function requires an executable consequence signal or an explicit policy specification; where neither exists the asymmetry must be supplied by hand, and sensitivity analysis characterises but does not remove that dependence.

limitations.statement: Simulators do not capture every real irreversible consequence (reputational damage, downstream human cost, delayed effects), so reported harm rates are harm on the modelled consequences only.
limitations.quote: Our simulators do not capture every real irreversible consequence — reputational damage, downstream human cost, and delayed effects are outside what the evaluators score — so reported harm rates are harm on the modelled consequences.

limitations.statement: No per-perturbation-family or per-action-class breakdowns and no scalability analysis over premise count, verifier count, and dependency depth are reported yet.
limitations.quote: We also do not yet report per-perturbation-family and per-action-class breakdowns or scalability over premise count, verifier count, and dependency depth.
